## Product Facts

- Mini Diarium is an encrypted offline journal for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Entries are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to the local SQLite database.
- The app is local-first and does not send entries to cloud services.
- Mini Diarium is a private diary app for desktop users who want local-only storage instead of a cloud account.
- Supported imports: Mini Diary JSON, Day One JSON/TXT, jrnl JSON.
- Supported exports: JSON and Markdown.

## Latest Articles

- A subpoena can only compel a company to hand over what it holds and can decrypt. A local-first journal with no server and no account has nothing to produce. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/can-your-journal-be-subpoenaed/)
- A password on a journal app can mean a login screen or real encryption at rest. Mini Diarium encrypts the whole journal with AES-256-GCM behind one password or key file, with a per-entry lock that prevents accidental edits, not a second password. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/password-protected-journal-app/)
- A secure journal app encrypts entries on disk with a named algorithm, has no recovery backdoor, and keeps a small network surface. Mini Diarium uses AES-256-GCM, has no HTTP client, and is open source for Windows, macOS, and Linux. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/secure-journal-app/)
- Notion stores journal entries on its servers, where AI features can read them. Mini Diarium encrypts each entry locally with AES-256-GCM, with no account and no server. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/notion-alternative-for-journaling/)
- Compares Mini Diarium to Obsidian for journal writing: Obsidian stores vault files as unencrypted Markdown on disk; Mini Diarium encrypts each entry with AES-256-GCM at the storage layer. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/obsidian-alternative-for-journaling/)
- Compares Mini Diarium to Standard Notes for users who want encrypted journal entries on their device only, with no sync service or server dependency. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/standard-notes-alternative/)
- A desktop diary app should encrypt entries at rest, store the primary copy locally, work offline, and export to open formats. Storage model and exit path matter more than feature lists. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/desktop-diary-app/)
- Five checks for evaluating a private journal app: encryption at rest, local storage, offline use, open exports, and open source. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/private-journal-app-how-to-choose/)
- An encrypted diary encrypts entries before they touch disk. It's an architectural guarantee, not a login screen. Here is what that means. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/what-is-an-encrypted-diary/)
- Explains why cloud architecture, not privacy settings, determines AI access to journal entries. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/journal-app-ai-privacy/)
- Mini Diary went unmaintained. Mini Diarium is its successor with AES-256-GCM encryption and direct import from Mini Diary JSON. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/mini-diary-alternative/)
- A practical checklist of what to look for in a journal app without cloud dependency. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/journal-app-without-cloud/)
- Compares Mini Diarium to Day One for users who want local-only storage and no sync service. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/day-one-alternative-for-private-offline-journaling/)
- An encrypted journal stores entries locally and encrypts before disk. Cloud apps store plaintext on servers. Architecture decides who can read your writing. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/encrypted-journal-vs-cloud-notes-app/)
- Owning your journal means keeping entries local, exporting in open formats, and never depending on a service for access. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/offline-journal-that-you-own/)
- A private diary app for desktop should encrypt entries at rest, work fully offline, and give you an exit path. Here is the checklist. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/private-diary-app-for-desktop/)
- Argues that local-first design is primarily about portability and long-term data control. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/local-first-journaling-and-ownership/)
- An offline journal can't send your entries to a server or share them with AI. That's architecture, not a setting. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/why-an-offline-journal-is-different/)
- The origin story of Mini Diarium: why an unmaintained predecessor led to building from scratch. (https://mini-diarium.com/blog/why-mini-diarium-exists/)

## Documentation

- Documentation hub: https://mini-diarium.com/docs/
- Getting Started: Create your first encrypted journal, set a password, and start writing. Covers the welcome tour, multiple journals, key file auth, and local-only mode. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/getting-started/)
- Writing Entries: Mini Diarium's rich text editor supports formatting, images, named links, tags, and multiple entries per day. Auto-save and RTL language support are built in. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/writing-entries/)
- Navigating Your Journal: Navigate your journal using the sidebar calendar, keyboard shortcuts, and day-navigation buttons. Jump to any date, go to today, and browse your entry history. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/navigating/)
- Search: Mini Diarium has full-text search across all encrypted entries. Learn how to find past entries with the search overlay and keyboard shortcut, and how searching stays fully encrypted and offline. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/search/)
- Importing Data: Import journal entries from Mini Diary, Day One, jrnl, or plain text files. Mini Diarium includes built-in importers and supports custom Rhai import plugins. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/import/)
- Exporting Data: Export your journal as JSON, Markdown, or PDF. JSON preserves IDs, tags, and metadata; Markdown is human-readable; PDF creates a formatted A4 document. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/export/)
- Plugins: Extend Mini Diarium with Rhai script plugins for custom import and export formats. Covers the plugins folder, writing your first plugin, and API helpers. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/plugins/)
- Preferences: Configure Mini Diarium from the Preferences panel: choose a theme, set auto-lock timeout, adjust editor font and size, manage authentication methods, and more. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/preferences/)
- Statistics: View your writing statistics: total entry and word counts, current and longest streaks, and a breakdown of your most active writing days, months, and years. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/statistics/)
- Backups: Mini Diarium automatically backs up your encrypted journal on every unlock and keeps the 30 most recent copies in a backups folder next to your diary.db. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/backups/)
- FAQ: Answers to common questions about Mini Diarium: password recovery, encryption model, cross-device sync, key files, authentication slots, and mobile support. (https://mini-diarium.com/docs/faq/)
